name: The Ferry Terminal and the Last Ferry

pages.name: The Ferry Terminal and the Last Ferry

text.content: Colman Dock and Puget Sound · Map: yes (terminal and ferry deck)

The terminal is almost empty. Under the fluorescents there's a handful of sleepy-faced passengers, a security guard staring at his phone, and a broken coffee machine. Outside, the last ferry of the night waits with its lights on and its engines running, like a white building floating on black water. The horn sounds once, long. Five minutes.

Structure: the terminal waiting room, the vehicle ramp, and the ferry: car deck, passenger cabin, bridge, and open stern deck.

The crossing to the far shore takes 35 minutes. Any conflict aboard has mortal witnesses locked in with the characters (Masquerade risk on every conspicuous roll).

Scene: @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}, the climax. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, @UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Gale}, or a courier tries to get the original of the File out of the city.

It's the “last boat of the night” from @UUID[JournalEntry.FVBnf3yE87K4BOhh]{Wendell Fry: “Song for the Son of the Fist”}.
